content: The data provided contains detailed information about tuberculosis (TB) prevalence surveys, diagnostic methods, and case definitions across various countries and years. TB Prevalence Surveys and Probable TB Cases 1. In Nigeria (2012), 144 total survey cases were recorded, with 22 probable TB cases identified. 2. In Vietnam (2007), 269 total survey cases were recorded, with 14 probable TB cases identified. 3. In Ethiopia (2011), 110 total survey cases were recorded, with 13 probable TB cases identified. 4. In Rwanda (2012), 40 total survey cases were recorded, with 13 probable TB cases identified. 5. In China (2010), 347 total survey cases were recorded, with 12 probable TB cases identified. 6. In the United Republic of Tanzania (2012), 134 total survey cases were recorded, with 10 probable TB cases identified. 7. In Thailand (2012), 142 total survey cases were recorded, with 8 probable TB cases identified. 8. In Gambia (2012), 77 total survey cases were recorded, with 8 probable TB cases identified. 9. In Pakistan (2011), 341 total survey cases were recorded, with 8 probable TB cases identified. 10. In Lao People's Democratic Republic (2011), 237 total survey cases were recorded, with 5 probable TB cases identified. 11. In Cambodia (2011), 314 total survey cases were recorded, with 4 probable TB cases identified. 12. In the Philippines (2007), 136 total survey cases were recorded, with 4 probable TB cases identified. 13. In Myanmar (2009), 311 total survey cases were recorded, with 2 probable TB cases identified. Note: Probable TB cases are defined as cases where Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) was not confirmed by culture but was identified either through two smear-positive slides or one smear-positive slide with a chest X-ray suggestive of TB. Diagnostic Algorithms and Laboratory Data Quality 1. Surveys using both Xpert assays and culture were conducted in selected countries, including Bangladesh, Kenya, the Philippines, Myanmar, Vietnam, and South Africa, between 2015 and 2019. 2. The diagnostic methods included solid culture media (Lowenstein-Jensen, LJ), liquid culture media (MGIT), and molecular diagnostics (Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert Ultra). 3. Index test results were interpreted without knowledge of reference standard results, minimizing bias. The likelihood of the reference standard correctly classifying the target condition was generally high, though some uncertainty existed in specific cases. 4. Culture contamination rates were within acceptable levels (2-5% for solid media, 8-10% for liquid media). The average time from sputum collection to culture inoculation was within 5 days in all cases. 5. Culture recovery from smear-positive specimens was below 95% in most cases, except where smear testing was not performed. 6. Evidence of culture cross-contamination was monitored using controls, with some laboratories achieving ISO 15189 accreditation and employing routine MGIT controls. Case Definitions in National TB Prevalence Surveys 1. South Africa (2017-2019): A single spot sample was collected for Xpert Ultra and MGIT. All culture-positive cases were considered survey cases, assuming no cross-contamination. If Xpert Ultra was positive but culture was negative, and the participant had no TB history, the case was included if chest X-ray findings were consistent with active TB (as determined by at least two out of three readers). 2. Lesotho (2019): A single spot sample was collected for Xpert Ultra and MGIT. Similar criteria to South Africa were applied for defining survey cases. 3. Eswatini (2018-2019): Two spot samples were collected for Xpert MTB/RIF in the field. If either was positive, additional samples were collected for culture. Cases were determined based on culture positivity and corresponding Xpert results. In cases of contamination or missing samples, a medical panel reviewed all available data. 4. Mozambique (2018-2020): A single spot sample was collected for Xpert MTB/RIF. If positive or invalid, another sample was tested. Cases without TB treatment history were defined based on Xpert positivity and chest X-ray findings. Cases with TB treatment history were excluded if culture results were negative. 5. Vietnam (2017-2018): A single spot sample was collected for Xpert MTB/RIF. If positive, a second sample was tested. All culture-positive cases were included, and Xpert-positive, culture-negative cases were included if chest X-ray findings were consistent with active TB. Sensitivity Comparisons of Diagnostic Methods 1. Sensitivity and specificity of Xpert Ultra and solid culture were compared using data from various countries, including Belarus, Brazil, and South Africa. 2. Sensitivity varied depending on smear status (positive or negative) and the number of specimens tested. 3. In Belarus, sensitivity for smear-positive specimens was higher than for smear-negative specimens. Similar trends were observed in Brazil and South Africa.
